definition: Multimodal sentiment analysis is a technology for traditional text-based sentiment analysis, which includes modalities such as audio and visual data.
details: It can be bimodal, which includes different combinations of two modalities, or trimodal, which incorporates three modalities. With the extensive amount of social media data available online in different forms such as videos and images, the conventional text-based sentiment analysis has evolved into more complex models of multimodal sentiment analysis, which can be applied in the development of virtual assistants, analysis of YouTube movie reviews, analysis of news videos, and emotion recognition (sometimes known as emotion detection) such as depression monitoring, among others. Similar to the traditional sentiment analysis, one of the most basic task in multimodal sentiment analysis is sentiment classification, which classifies different sentiments into categories such as positive, negative, or neutral. The complexity of analyzing text, audio, and visual features to perform such a task requires the application of different fusion techniques, such as feature-level, decision-level, and hybrid fusion. The performance of these fusion techniques and the classification algorithms applied, are influenced by the type of textual, audio, and visual features employed in the analysis.

explainer.lead: Multimodal sentiment analysis reads emotion from text together with audio and visual signals rather than text alone, which matters because tone and facial expression carry sentiment that words miss. It has grown with the volume of video and image data posted online.

tiers.eli5: Instead of judging how someone feels from their words only, it also listens to their voice and watches their face, like noticing a friend says "I'm fine" while frowning.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fuse text, audio, and visual features in bimodal or trimodal models depending on which signals are available. A common pitfall is relying on one modality dominating the fused representation, or on modalities that are missing at inference time.
tiers.paperLevel: A model takes one or more modalities as input and predicts a sentiment label or score; variants are bimodal (two modalities) or trimodal (three). Performance is bounded by the quality and alignment of each modality's data.

explainer.example: A YouTube movie review video is scored not only on the reviewer's words but also on vocal tone and facial expressions, combining all three modalities in a trimodal model.
